messages:
devon: Heads up — after the continuous-batching heuristic roll at 09:12 UTC we’re seeing p99 token latency ~2x on small requests (<=64 tokens). Throughput also down on high-concurrency tails.
sre-bot: ALERT: runtime-prod p99-token-latency > threshold (2.1s) for service=redwood-inference-runtime
ana: I mean ana: I’m looking at traces now, grabbing a few profiles.
matt: which change specifically went out? last PR was tune/token-budget-targets and queue-policy tweaks.
devon: PR #4592 — adjusted token_budget_target from 64->128 and enabled queue_policy=adaptive_warmup.
lee: quick glance at batch distribution from 09:10-09:40: mean_batch_size dropped to 1.8, 68% of batches <4. That combined with larger token_budget means more flush/wait churn.
ana: dumping a short profile (aggregated 5m window):
```
profile_summary:
  kernel_selection:
    fused_attn_small_seq: calls=86k, avg_startup=1.1ms
    aten_gemm_fast: calls=32k, avg_startup=0.3ms
  batch_stats:
    mean_batch_size: 1.8
    pct_batches_<4: 68
  queue_metrics:
    avg_queue_time: 12ms -> 45ms (post-roll)
    token_budget_target: 128
  kv_cache:
    hit_rate: 0.72
    avg_kv_fetch_ms: 0.9
```
ana: Interesting — kernel selection moved more small-seq work to fused_attn_small_seq which has higher per-call startup. With tiny batches the startup dominates.
sarah: So higher token_budget to wait for tokens backfired because the traffic is many independent single-turn requests; we end up waiting then falling back to small fused kernel repeatedly.
johannes: Also noticed a spike in queue depth variance. Some requests waited ~60ms then processed solo. That explains latency but why throughput drop?
devon: When many requests wait for budget, we serialize startup overheads instead of filling batches; end-to-end GPU utilization dips.
matt: Can we toggle kernel preference to favor aten_gemm_fast for seq_len<=32 as a temporary mitigation?
ana: We can, but that bypasses fused_attn for small seq. Might reduce p99 but could increase avg token cost.
sre-bot: Deploy bot log: deploy #4592 -> continuous-batching:v2 enabled @ 09:12 by matt
matt: Rolling back the feature flag for prod now (continuous-batching:v2 -> off).
deploy-bot: rollback initiated: deploy #4592 -> revert at 09:46 by matt
lee: Early telemetry after rollback (09:46-09:58): p99 token latency trending down, queue_time back to ~10ms, mean_batch_size ~2.1.
ana: Quick A/B test suggestion: run a canary with token_budget_target=96 and queue_policy=latency_first for 10% of traffic, collect p99 & throughput.
johannes: Also add a metric to capture kernel_switch_count per-request so we can see how often we flip kernels mid-run.
sarah: Recording follow-ups: (1) revert in prod confirmed, (2) run canary with smaller token target, (3) add kernel_switch_count metric + per-seq kernel latency.
devon: I’ll open a concise postmortem and include the profiling artifacts + the perf repro script. Assigning action owners: ana -> kernel metric, johannes -> canary config, matt -> postmortem writeup + cost/latency tradeoff notes.
matt: TL;DR — heuristic change increased token_budget assuming batching would improve throughput. On low-latency, many single-turn requests, it increased wait + favored a higher-startup kernel causing p99 regression. Rollback helped.
ana: For the postmortem I attached this small repro command to simulate traffic mix:
```
# reproduce: mix of small single-turn requests + multi-turn
./perf-runner --rate 1200 --mix "70:single_32,30:multi_256" --seed 42 --record kernel_selection,queue_time
```
lee: FYI I flagged an infra dashboard anomaly: gpu_util decreased by ~12% during the window. Saved a screenshot.
sre-bot: Incident closed? Awaiting human confirmation.
devon: closing: yes, rollback restored baseline. Opening postmortem doc and linking perf traces. Will schedule follow-up to iterate on smarter kernel selection policy (prefer low-startup kernel under high single-turn fraction).
matt: thanks everyone. leave the canary config ready; let's test token_budget range [48,96] before re-enabling any global change. :thumbsup:
